# API Map

Repo-wide entry points and the formal public-API tracking rules. Layer-specific surfaces (compiler error codes, IDE diagnostic IDs, extensibility patterns) live in the path-scoped instruction files:
- Compiler error codes, `MessageID`, Syntax/BoundNodes, codegen, `csc`/`vbc` → `.github/instructions/Compiler.instructions.md`
- IDE diagnostic IDs, MEF service/analyzer/code-fix exports, LSP → `.github/instructions/IDE.instructions.md`

## Build & Test Entry Points

| Command | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `build.sh` / `Build.cmd` | Full solution build (Arcade). |
| `dotnet build Compilers.slnf` | Compiler-only build. |
| `dotnet build Ide.slnf` | IDE-only build. |
| `dotnet build Razor.slnf` | Razor compiler & tooling-only build. |
| `test.sh` / `Test.cmd` | Full test run. |
| `dotnet test <test.csproj>` | Run a specific test project. |
| `dotnet run --file eng/generate-compiler-code.cs` | Regenerate Syntax/BoundNodes code. |
| `pwsh eng/validate-benchmarks.ps1 -configuration Release -ci` | Validate benchmark projects with BenchmarkDotNet Dry jobs; custom multi-job Razor harnesses use their explicit validation mode. Used by the correctness artifacts CI job. |
| `artifacts/bin/BuildBoss/<config>/net472/BuildBoss.exe -r <repo>/ -c <config> -p Roslyn.slnx` | Validate solutions, project files and build artifacts. Used by the correctness artifacts CI job and the bootstrap build. See `src/Tools/BuildBoss/README.md` for available checks and options. |
| `pwsh eng/validate-roslyn-sdk-samples.ps1 -configuration Release -ci` | Verifies every project under `src/RoslynSdk/Samples/` is included in the standalone `RoslynSdkSamples.slnx` sample solution (catching new/removed sample projects that weren't added to or removed from it), then builds that solution with `--warnaserror /p:RoslynEnforceCodeStyle=true` to confirm the samples actually compile *and* pass this repo's Roslyn code-style analyzers with zero warnings — so this is also the lint/code-style gate for every Roslyn SDK sample, not just a compile check. Used by the correctness artifacts CI job (`azure-pipelines.yml`). |
| `dotnet msbuild <proj> /t:UpdateXlf` | Refresh `.xlf` after `.resx` changes. |
| `folly.ps1 <attune\|weave\|bind\|scry> [Debug\|Release] [--core\|--framework] [--binaryLog] [--verbosity <level>]` (Windows) / `folly.sh <attune\|weave\|bind\|scry> [Debug\|Release] [--binaryLog] [--verbosity <level>]` (Linux/macOS) | This fork's wrapper around `eng/build.ps1`/`eng/build.sh` for `FollyOfTheUnbound.slnx`: `attune` restores, `weave` restores+builds, `bind` restores+builds+packs (via the real Arcade toolset, not a bare `dotnet build`/`pack`, which bypasses this repo's SDK bootstrap). `bind` also copies the produced nupkgs to `../.nupkg/FotU/<Configuration>`. `scry` restores+builds+tests, but the two wrappers differ here: `folly.sh scry` only runs Core tests (no `net472` runtime on Linux/macOS to run Framework tests against, so it has no `--core`/`--framework` equivalent), while `folly.ps1 scry` runs both a Core pass and a Framework pass by default, each writing straight to its own `-Core`/`-Framework`-suffixed `artifacts/TestResults`/`artifacts/log` directory via `FOTU_TEST_RESULTS_SUFFIX` (read by `eng/build.ps1`'s `TestUsingRunTests`, which forwards it as RunTests' `--out`/`--logs`) so the two passes' same-named result files never collide -- `--core`/`--framework` restrict it to just one pass, and `--timeout <minutes>` overrides RunTests' whole-run `--timeout` watchdog (default 90; both wrappers now forward `-testTimeout`/`--testTimeout` to `eng/build.ps1`/`eng/build.sh`, which fall back to 90 when it's unset and Helix isn't in use). `-testInteractiveConsole` is passed unconditionally, for every pass, always -- so RunTests inherits the real console directly and its live per-work-item progress table (`LiveTestProgressDisplay`, drawn in the terminal's alternate screen buffer -- see `src/Tools/RunTests/LiveTestProgressDisplay.cs`) always prints live, for both passes when both run. This is deliberate, not an oversight: `Console.IsOutputRedirected` is a one-way flag `LiveTestProgressDisplay.TryCreate` checks once up front, so piping a pass's output through the PowerShell pipeline at all -- even just to relay it back out line-by-line -- permanently costs that pass its real live table, with no way to "un-redirect" it back afterward; only the plain scrolling fallback RunTests uses outside a real terminal remains. Getting a single combined final-results view without that cost needed a RunTests-side change: `-testSuppressConsoleSummary` (forwarded to RunTests' own `--suppressConsoleSummary`, see `Options.SuppressConsoleSummary`) suppresses only `TestRunner.Print`'s final PASSED/FAILED/TIMEOUT table from the console -- the live table is untouched, and the table is still written to that pass's log file regardless (`ConsoleUtil`/`Logger` always log what they print, console-suppressed or not). `folly.ps1` passes this only when both passes are requested together: each pass's own final table would otherwise print live the moment that pass finishes and get buried under the other pass's subsequent build/live-progress output, so instead both passes' tables are read back from `runtestsCore.log`/`runtestsFramework.log` (RunTests' `Program.WriteLogFile` names the file after `Options.TestRuntime` precisely so the two passes' otherwise-identically-named log files never collide when collected together) once everything finishes and printed together in one `=== <Pass> results ===`-per-pass combined block, immediately followed by a compact combined numeric recap (`=== Test summary ===`). A single-leg run passes neither pass `-testSuppressConsoleSummary`, so its one table just prints live as normal and there's nothing to combine. `--binaryLog` forwards to `eng/build.ps1`/`eng/build.sh`'s own `-binaryLog`/`--binaryLog`, writing `Build.binlog` under `artifacts/log/<Configuration>/`; `--verbosity <level>` forwards MSBuild console verbosity (`quiet`\|`minimal`\|`normal`\|`detailed`\|`diagnostic` -- full words only, not MSBuild's own `q`/`m`/`n`/`d`/`diag` shorthand). Neither is valid with `cleanse` (there's no build to log); `reflection` (see below) rejects both alongside its own "no primary arg or switches" rule. `scry --collectDumps` (both wrappers) forwards RunTests' `--collectdumps`, which enables `DumpUtil.EnableRegistryDumpCollection` (`src/Tools/RunTests/ProcDumpUtil.cs`), a Windows Error Reporting registry-based mechanism (`HKLM\...\LocalDumps`, requires Administrator) with no cross-platform equivalent -- `eng/build.ps1`'s `IsWindowsPlatform` / `eng/build.sh`'s `is_windows_host` skip it with a note off a genuine Windows host rather than erroring. **Deliberately opt-in, not scry's default**: this mutates a single machine-wide registry key with no cross-process coordination (two concurrent elevated `scry` runs race it), and RunTests' own timeout-dump path (`Program.HandleTimeout`/`ProcessUtil.GetTestHostProcesses`) sweeps every testhost-like process on the machine, not just this run's -- both are fine for a caller who explicitly asked for dump collection, not as a silent default for every ordinary local run. `DumpUtil` saves and restores whatever was previously in that key (value and `RegistryValueKind`, read with `DoNotExpandEnvironmentNames` so a `REG_EXPAND_SZ` `DumpFolder` isn't flattened) rather than deleting it, so a single run at least doesn't clobber a developer's own pre-existing WER config. `--procdumppath` (from `Ensure-ProcDump`/`EnsureProcDump`, which downloads Procdump.zip from sysinternals.com on a machine without a cached `procdump.exe`) is independent of `--collectdumps` and only ever feeds RunTests' console `"Proc dump location:"` line (`Program.RunAsync`) -- nothing functional consumes it -- so a download failure (offline machine, blocked network) drops only that cosmetic value, never `--collectdumps` itself. |
| `folly.ps1 cleanse` / `folly.sh cleanse` | Deletes `artifacts/` via a single bulk `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force`/`rm -rf` (backgrounded, with a throttled byte/count progress display), after first stopping two independent kinds of lingering process that can hold a DLL open under `artifacts/` and block the delete on Windows: (1) `dotnet build-server shutdown` for a registered VBCSCompiler/MSBuild/Razor build server, and (2) a direct pattern-match-and-kill of any process whose command line references both this repo's own `.dotnet` SDK root and `MSBuild.dll`, for an MSBuild node-reuse worker left behind by a build/test invocation outside `folly` (build servers and node-reuse workers are separate mechanisms -- see `KNOWN_ISSUES.md`). Either step prints what it actually stopped/killed, or nothing if there was nothing to report. Exit code is a real success/failure contract, not just a summary: **exits 0** only if `artifacts/` no longer exists afterward (including "there was nothing to clean" and "it existed only as a file/symlink and got removed"); **exits 1** whenever anything survives -- a locked file, a permission-denied subtree, or any other leftover -- after one bulk-delete retry. In the exit-1 case the summary line distinguishes an exact survivor count from an uncertain one (`"at least N ... (some may be unreadable and not counted)"`) when the scan itself couldn't fully traverse the remaining tree. Both wrappers exit identically here; this is intentional lockstep behavior, not incidental overlap (see the `folly.sh`/`folly.ps1` parity rule in `CONVENTIONS.md`). |

Solution filters: `Roslyn.slnx` (full), `Compilers.slnf`, `Ide.slnf`, `Razor.slnf`, `FollyOfTheUnbound.slnx` (this fork's Compilers+IDE+Razor filter, excluding most of `RoslynAnalyzers`).

## Public API Tracking

- Every public-API addition/change must update the owning project's `PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt`.
- Enforced by the PublicApiAnalyzer (e.g., `RS0016` for undeclared public API). Promote entries to `PublicAPI.Shipped.txt` at release/snap time.

## Resource Strings

- Strings live in `.resx`, accessed via generated designer classes (`CSharpResources`, `FeaturesResources`, `AnalyzersResources`, …).
- After editing a `.resx`, run `dotnet msbuild <project.csproj> /t:UpdateXlf` to refresh `.xlf` files.
